newsitem.title: UK: Burger King holds out before buying UK beef.
newsitem.headline: Burger King holds out before buying UK beef.

text.p: Fast-food chain Burger King, owned by UK food and drinks giant Grand Metropolitan, said on Thursday it was awaiting a "tangible upturn in consumer confidence" before buying British beef.
"There are still a number of our customers who have concerns," a company spokeswoman told Reuters. "We hope to see that number decreasing so we can take the decision to go back into British beef."
She said she was encouraged by a slow but steady rise in consumer confidence, according to research carried out by the company on a weekly basis.

But she noted that it was too soon to speculate when the company may decide to buy British beef again amid concerns that so-called "mad cow" disease, which has beset British herds, can infect humans with the fatal brain wasting condition called Creutzfeld Jakob Disease (CJD).
Burger King was commenting just minutes before American fast-food giant McDonald's Corp said it had decided to buy British beef again for its hamburgers.

Burger King, which is meeting British farm minister Jack Cunningham next Tuesday, said it had never used British beef for 100 percent of its UK hamburgers because the amount of the quality they needed had never been available.
But the company stopped buying any British beef, opting instead for continental European beef, at the end of March last year.
"We've continued not to use British beef but it's very much something we'd like to. The question of consumer confidence is at the root of all our actions," the spokeswoman said.
Burger King is conducting its next consumer research this weekend. The results will be available early next week.
